items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Gunther Schuller was here just a few months ago. He has a new biography that just came out... And he gave a kind of Q & A session with all the jazz students for an hour

ctx.x: I was going to ask you about that. Because we’ve been talking about the 70s and I read your interview with your son, or part of it, and you specifically mentioned the 70s as a significant decade for the downfall of culture. I mean I’m paraphrasing you, but you had an attitude about that. And do you remember what specifically —

Well I think a lot of what it has to do with is something that you can apply to so many areas today and that relates to everything from ecological crisis to medical and social issues and all kinds of things, the difference between organic and synthetic. And I think up until the explosion of technological media, which took place mostly after the mass marketing of television, pop music and music for most of the general public became more and more something that had not really developed in an organic way. It’s…

Well you’ve said a few other things, not only about the 70s, but this is a leap to present day, but you sound fairly pessimistic about American culture in general, and especially having an experience in Germany and how they support the arts. And I liked this one thing. I think you were talking about the United States. You say, “You can afford a lot of worthwhile things if you’re not trying to run the world.”
